Aldric Marrow.narrative: I am the Reeve of Brackenford, and I have kept this town's ledger for thirty years. The gate-due pays the guards who keep the road clear of wolves and outlaws, and I will not see it dropped for Kettlebridge coin. I took the Coldwell fields for the town store when the Hales could not pay, and I outlawed them when they would not leave. My son Tobin shamed me before Josiah Crane, and Mercy Abbot would sell the town's safety for trade. I am old, and I have not named who comes after me.
goals: clear the outlaws from the stone road

memories.gist: The Lean Year: I lent grain to Thornby and to Coldwell against their next harvests, and took the Coldwell fields when they could not pay.
The broken match: Tobin broke his promise to Hester Crane and married Wenna, and I was shamed before Josiah Crane.
The day I outlawed Marta Hale and her household at the gate.
Mercy Abbot stood in the square and called the gate-due robbery; I told her it pays the guards.
I wrote Thornby's debt in the ledger myself, forty baskets, and it has not been cleared.

stances.why: It pays the guards who keep the road clear of wolves and outlaws.
The Hales could not pay, and the town store took the fields lawfully.
She would drop the due for Kettlebridge coin and leave the road unguarded.
The ledger is the town's memory; Thornby's debt is not forgotten.
He broke his promise to Hester Crane and married Wenna.

Cuth Marrow.narrative: I am Aldric's wife, and I keep a quiet house while he keeps the town. I tend the sick with the chapel sisters, and I have seen more of Brackenford's troubles than my husband knows. The gate-due and the Coldwell business are his to settle, but I wish the town would stop talking about Wenna. I am not a woman of many words, but I know what I know.
goals: soften Aldric's temper if I can

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is stubborn, but he is mine.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: son

relations.name: Maud Marrow
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She works hard under her father's eye.

relations.name: Wenna Marrow
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She is carrying my first grandchild, and the town is unkind.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We tend the sick together; she is a steady hand.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: She will deliver Wenna's child, and she knows her trade.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: I nursed her son through a fever; she is not a monster.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She and my husband quarrel, but she means well for the town.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: cook
relations.note: She is Marta's sister, but she keeps her peace at the inn.

relations.name: Sister Perrin
relations.label: chapel sister
relations.note: She keeps the common fire and the feast days faithfully; I would trust her with the calendar and the hearth both.

memories.gist: I tended Marta Hale's son through a fever at Coldwell last winter, and she let me in.
The Lean Year: I helped feed the town from the store and watched the Hales lose their fields.
Tobin's wedding to Wenna: a small affair, and half the town did not come.
I sat with Joan Hobson through a long birth and learned a thing or two.

stances.why: I tend anyone who comes, outlaw or not.
Wenna is my son's wife, and the town's talk is cruel.
I keep the house so Aldric can keep the town.
It is Aldric's business, though I wish it did not split the square.

Maud Marrow.narrative: I am the Reeve's daughter, and I keep the market rolls and the gate ledger under my father's eye. I am not a girl any more, and I know the ledger better than he thinks. Mercy Abbot asks for copies when my father is asleep, and I give them, because I believe the gate-due does more harm than good. I have not told my father, and I do not know what he would do if he knew.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: father
relations.note: He trusts me with the rolls, but not with my own mind.

relations.name: Cuth Marrow
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the house quiet and knows more than she says.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: brother

relations.name: Wenna Marrow
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She did not ask for the town's talk.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot

relations.name: Pernel Pip

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: guard

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He hates the due, and I do not blame him.

memories.gist: The first time Mercy Abbot asked me for a copy of the gate ledger, and I agreed.
The Lean Year: I wrote the Coldwell fields into the town store's ledger, and my father signed it.
Tobin broke the match with Hester Crane, and the town talked of nothing else for a month.
I copied the Thornby debt entry for my father, forty baskets, and he said it would not be forgotten.

stances.why: I see the carters' faces when they pay it.
The rolls should be accurate and known, not hidden.
If he knew I copied for Mercy, he would never trust me again.
She wants trade back, and she is not a fool.

Maud Marrow.secret: Copies the ledger for Mercy Abbot when her father is asleep.
